entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: A=sanke noka a=nuye uske or ta, tan noka harkisama ta an tuyka un sikkewe anu yan. X newa Y anak 0, 1, 2, 3, … pixel ne; 0 wano a=piski. Mosma noka sinep sinep anak tane a=anu uske or ta an. Te ta noka a=ukaomare yakka pirka; oka ta a=omare noka anak hoski a=omare noka ka ta a=nuye. A=ari noka opitta onnay ta oka kuni, noka a=nuye uske poro. A=tuye uske newa noka kor pororu anak a=sinnare ka somo ki.
entries.note: All English clauses were compared with the actual Ainu paragraph. The top-left phrase has competing modifier attachment: harkisama ta an precedes tuyka un sikkewe, without securely demonstrating that both directions identify one corner of this image. The bare list-plus-pixel copular predicate does not explicitly select one integer value for each coordinate; intended set-membership relies on notation and context. Current-position an is plausible but less explicit about invariance. Permission, plural placement/existence and bare purpose kuni are independently supported and are not errors. Novel output-canvas and crop/size phrases remain technical extensions. These whole-value gaps prevent acceptance even though import ordering and expansion intent are recoverable. In the expansion purpose clause, onnay has no explicit canvas possessor; the immediately preceding placed-images noun phrase also admits a locative attachment. The logical roles of all images as subject and canvas as containing region need clearer confirmation. Valid purpose kuni alone cannot close this gap.

G1.type: Primary published Saru grammar by Tamura Suzuko
G1.evidence: Sections 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7: prenominal modifiers, nominal possession with kor where appropriate, locatives, indefinite-person marking, number, copular predicates, and imperative yan. Used to evaluate syntax, not as attestation of the new UI prose.

A1.evidence: harkisam is left side, harkisama its relational/possessed counterpart. Physical left is supported; no reading-direction interpretation is needed.

A2.evidence: tuyka includes an upper end and is expressly distinguished from a table or paper surface, ka. This supports the physical-edge versus stacking distinction, not the full nested top-left phrase.

A3.evidence: sikkew/sikkewe denotes a corner; the possessed example explicitly attaches to the object whose corner it is. Does not demonstrate the draft’s two-level directional modifier.

A4.evidence: Placement verb anu, including the complete polite command anu yan. Relative place phrases additionally checked against uske.

A5.evidence: uske is a modified place expression. Independently attested an uske supports location phrasing; this is no claim that a coordinate-label expression is lexicalized.

A6.evidence: Instrumental/means ani includes a measuring-instrument example. Applying it to a unit, pixel, is a transparent technical extension assessed in the complete X/Y labels.

A7.evidence: The starting point can be spatial or temporal; wano is not restricted to time. Supports physical-origin captions and the intended zero origin.

A8.evidence: Transitive choose/select; an attested relative clause a=numke a kur directly supports the selected-item construction. Selection from an abstract enumerated numeric domain remains an application not attested here.

A9.evidence: Absence/nonexistence; Kayano explicitly uses tane isam for something formerly present but now gone.

A10.evidence: Similarity/correspondence expressions, including doing according to words; koracipo is an intensified comparison. They do not by themselves establish numerical-exactness terminology.

A11.evidence: Sense 2 is explicitly purpose. Sense 3 also permits following ne for intended/expected state. Therefore neither bare purpose kuni nor terminal kuni ne is rejected as inherently ungrammatical. Whether the latter adequately imposes a validation requirement is a separate UI judgment.

A12.evidence: yakka pirka is expressly permission, so the overlap clause has a supported permissive construction.

A13.evidence: Placement ari is plural and has singular anu. It is not only the homophonous fire-lighting verb.

A14.evidence: Plural existence is distinguished from relational after/behind. Supports the canvas-purpose plural; temporal oka ta must still be interpreted with its contextual comparison.

A15.evidence: poro can mean becoming larger as well as being large, so expansion is a supported reading rather than a mechanically forced backtranslation.

A16.evidence: Kayano has a drawing example with noka as design/object; Tamura warns that the traditionally marked surface is often the object. The draft’s image-drawing extension is possible, but cannot be certified merely from the gloss write.

A17.evidence: sinep sinep is explicitly distributive, one by one. This removes an alleged automatic an/oka mismatch but does not independently add continuance to the whole clause.

A18.evidence: piski counts objects. Integer-domain membership is not established by this word alone.

A19.evidence: or supplies a locative relation to a preceding referent; or wa also has an agentive use. The numeric-list construction must be justified as a collection-source reading, not inferred solely from the gloss from.

C1.type: Published community terminology collection; primary evidence of this collection’s proposals, not linguistic authority
C1.evidence: Payload directly has cipiskip number, omare import and sanke export attributed to a translation collection; pororu size is explicitly tagged neologism. Thus these are not newly invented by this patch, but publication does not establish broad acceptance.

A20.evidence: The complete entry is transitive combine one on top of another. The image-overlap application has clear stacking support; it is not a claim of a standardized digital-overlap term.

A21.evidence: onnay is the interior of a referent; the possessed form is onnayke. Actual locative examples supply a container. The draft’s purpose clause leaves the canvas container implicit after a preceding images NP, creating a reference/attachment question not answered by the word interior alone.

A22.evidence: noka explicitly includes image, design, likeness and model. The unknown-image message is therefore not accepted solely by borrowing catalogue usage.

A23.evidence: An intensified comparison corresponding to exactly like/as. This supplies the replacement title’s proposed word but does not certify that whole title.

important_negative_findings: Do not reject bare purpose kuni: the primary dictionary explicitly attests that use.
Do not treat poro as only static large: become larger is attested.
Do not reject the permission formula yakka pirka or plural ari/oka: both are supported.
No Latin/Kana mismatch was detected; correct pairing does not clear whole-value linguistic holds.
No dictionary equivalent is required for every composed UI phrase, but the particular unresolved constructions cannot be promoted on hashes, glosses or backtranslation alone.
remaining_limits: Title: numerical-exactness reading of comparison to written numeric values.
Help: nested/appositional upper-left corner reference, per-coordinate numeric-list membership, and complete idiomatic technical prose.
Validation: collection-source construction for the finite numeric domain and unambiguous normative force.
Newa has evidence outside the particular Saru materials inspected; no blanket claim that it is invalid Ainu is made.
Published modern terminology is evidence of a proposal, not broad community or native approval.
Expansion: explicitly distinguish placed images as the subject and drawing area as the container of onnay, rather than treating lexical purpose support as full-sentence approval.
source_access: Web grammar read successfully. Some dictionary URL opens returned retrieval errors, so ordinary HTTPS reads were used without bypassing any denied access. Temporary shell transport failure recovered.
